issue.body:
**Evidence:** [`2026-10-09-supply-providers-and-transfer-clamps.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-09-supply-providers-and-transfer-clamps.md) §2 (cases Ta1–Ta4, Tb1, Tc1–Tc2: Wine, played; `TFleetToFleet` handlers `0x443924` / `0x443b48`: code), now confirmed as the settled reading by the [manual consolidation](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-22-manual133-contradictions-consolidated.md) item 2 and the correction note on UF03 in [`2026-10-08-unit-map-fleet-uf01-uf06.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-08-unit-map-fleet-uf01-uf06.md) (research `08c023f..df8b6a9`). The "There are more than 100 ships in these fleets combined." box belongs to Join fleets (R15) only.

**The original (Transfer ships):**
- **No refusal at all.** The ship arrow moves `min(step, ships left on the giver, 100 − ships on the receiver)`, so the receiver stops at 100 (Tb1: 95 + 8 offered → 100 / 5), and OK applies. No box.
- **No army or capacity test.** A carrying fleet can give or take ships, and can end below its army's needs (Ta2: 20 ships carrying 10,700 troops).
- **Emptying a carrying fleet deletes its army silently** (Ta4: the fleet and army 0 tombstoned, 10,700 troops lost, no prompt). Its money and supplies go to the other fleet first (already matched, #962).

**The remake**, `src/IC2.Engine/Naval/Commands/FleetToFleetTransferCommandHandler.cs`:
- `:85–:89` refuses when **either fleet carries an army** (`naval.carrying-army`); the command's remarks (`FleetToFleetTransferCommand.cs:25–:36`, T46 DoD 2) chose this to avoid stranding an army with a dangling `AboardFleetId`.
- `:131–:136` refuses a combined count over `JoinMaxShips` with **Join fleets' text** (`naval.combined-ships-too-large`), marked `[designed]` because "no report states whether `TFleetToFleet` enforces" the cap (`FleetToFleetTransferCommand.cs:52–:62`); a report now does.

**Expected under `classical-faithful`:** (a) a transfer to a carrying fleet, or a partial transfer from one, is accepted with no capacity test; (b) the 100-ship ceiling is a clamp, not a refusal with a box (the Godot dialog's stepper stopping at `100 − receiver` is enough; the engine may clamp or reject a programmatic over-request, but never shows the Join text); (c) what happens when a carrying fleet gives all its ships is a **design decision for the owner**: the report calls the silent army loss "likely an original defect the remake need not copy". Options include copying it under `classical-faithful`, refusing only that last-ship case, or moving the army to the receiving fleet. Removing the army needs the carrier unlink the remake already does for conquered fleets, so the save stays valid.

**Also stale:** `docs/game-design.md`'s "Fleet management" bullet said none of the fleet orders work while carrying an army; corrected on branch `evidence/2026-10-22-manual-review`. `docs/investigations/v062-user-manual.md` (`:131`) describes the remake's current behaviour and stays right until this changes.

Found by the stage-2 evaluation of the research reports of 2026-10-22.
